title: August 2026 fresh-intake production - batch H3B-1, the technical and operational roots
note: SEVEN ROOTS IN, FIVE NEW CARDS AND ONE EXPANSION OUT. The governing brief named seven technical/operational roots. Two of them did not need a new card and the evidence for that is recorded below rather than asserted. WHAT THE GOVERNED ADJUDICATION STORE GOT WRONG. Every root already carried a classification in AUGUST2026_INTAKE_ADJUDICATIONS.json, and those classifications were scored against a 738-card corpus. The corpus is now 752, so every negative search in them is stale by fourteen cards, and one of them was wrong at the time it was written. AUG-0146 (angle of repose) was classified GENUINE_NEW_QUESTION on the evidence that "regex 'angle of repose' returns 0 hits over 738 cards, independently re-confirmed". That is false. The same regex over tag-stripped card text returns SEVEN pre-existing cards - QB2_A#q10, #q11, #q13, #q27, #q28, #q29 and QB2_B#q15 - none of which was created after that adjudication. QB2_A#q27 already defines the term in a trap question and QB2_B#q15 already carries the 35-degree threshold. A new root would have been card explosion. The disposition is therefore EXISTING_CARD_EXPANSION on QB2_B#q15, and the adjudication's evidence line is contradicted here on the record rather than quietly worked around. This is the ORB negative-search failure repeating in a different file: it is not enough for a pattern to return zero, the pattern has to be able to match the way the corpus writes the thing, and someone has to open the likely cards. AUG-0166 (structural diagrams) was already correctly classified PARAPHRASE_EXISTING against QB1_K#q6. That card was read in full and it answers the ask completely - it is titled 'List the plans onboard related to ship structure' and gives the whole set grouped as geometry, structure, strength and loading, damage and emergency, and survey-support records. EXISTING_CARD_SUFFICIENT, no edit. A CONTRADICTION INSIDE THE STORE, RESOLVED. AUG-0136 ('how to prevent container fire as a chief engineer') is classified GENUINE_NEW_QUESTION while AUG-0219 ('how to prevent container fire, then he went into asking about IMDG') is classified PARAPHRASE_EXISTING against QB2_A#q8. Those are the same ask and cannot both be right. QB2_A#q8 was read in full: it is titled 'Container deck fire - major reasons, EmS structure, and firefighting procedure' and it is a RESPONSE card. It gives root causes, the EmS schedule structure and the firefighting procedure; it does not give the Chief Engineer's prevention programme. So the prevention ask is genuinely unanswered and both occurrences are recorded against the new card, with AUG-0219's IMDG limb cross-linked to the existing QB2_A#q9. CURRENCY WORK THAT CHANGED THE CONTENT. Two findings would have made these cards stale on the day they shipped. (1) IGF Code paragraph 18.4.1.1.1 was REPLACED by resolution MSC.551(108), adopted 23 May 2024, accepted 1 July 2025, IN FORCE 1 JANUARY 2026. The pre-transfer written agreement now covers five items, not three - it gained minimum and maximum limiting transfer pressure and temperature, and bunkering line PRV settings. The corpus held only MSC.391(95), MSC.422(98) and MSC.458(101), and an answer written from those alone would have been the H1 BMP5 failure exactly: authoritative base, stale for the one provision being taught. MSC.567(109) (in force 1 January 2028) was also read and does NOT touch chapter 8, 18.4 or the BDN annex, and the card says so. (2) CONTAINER FIRE - AND THIS RECORD GOT IT WRONG THE FIRST TIME. The dedicated containership fire DETECTION AND CONTROL amendments to SOLAS chapter II-2 and the FSS Code are still draft, and that much was right. But the first version of the card, and of this note, swept the FIREFIGHTING EQUIPMENT into the same bucket and told candidates that water mist lances, mobile monitors and hold drenchers were company practice rather than SOLAS. That is false and it was caught in independent review. SOLAS II-2 reg. 10.7.3.1 provides that ships constructed on or after 1 January 2016 designed to carry containers on or above the weather deck SHALL CARRY at least one water mist lance, and 10.7.3.2 requires mobile water monitors - at least two under 30 m breadth, at least four at 30 m and above - where five or more tiers are carried on deck. Reg. 19.3.1.3 requires the under-deck cargo space to be cooled at at least 5 L/min per square metre by fixed spraying nozzles or by flooding, which is the provision people call the drencher. All three were read from the IMO SOLAS Consolidated Edition 2024 after the review raised them. The card now teaches the boundary the other way round and its trap question, which had scripted the wrong answer to 'is a water mist lance required by SOLAS?', now answers YES. Section 14 of the brief says not to imply prevention technology that is not mandatory; the opposite failure - denying equipment that IS mandatory - is worse, because a candidate who denies it is contradicted by his own ship's certificate. LOCAL CORPUS REUSE. Nothing here started from a web search. IGF chapter 8, chapter 18.4 and the LNG Bunker Delivery Note annex were read from MSC.391(95) held in the shared true-source corpus; MSC.422(98) and MSC.458(101) were read from the same folder and cleared. SOLAS II-2 regulation 19.2.2, 19.3.1 to 19.3.8 and 19.4 were read from the IMO SOLAS Consolidated Edition 2024 held in official-sources, and the two chapter II-2 amendments in force since that edition, MSC.520(106) and MSC.550(108), were read from the corpus and neither amends regulation 19. The IMDG amendment number and date came from MSC.556(108), held locally. Only MSC.551(108) and MSC.567(109) had to be retrieved, and they were retrieved from IMO's own resolution index and read as bytes. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED. No universal numerical angle of repose (the 35 degrees is a Code threshold, not a cargo property). No IMO methane number - that is the engine maker's figure and the card says so. No regulation for Pareto analysis - the card states plainly that no IMO instrument requires it. No Maersk-specific procedure anywhere. No casualty is named where the card could not source one; the container-fire and digitalisation casualty sections give the generalisable pattern instead and say that is what they are doing. INDEPENDENT REVIEW. COMPLETE - THREE CLEAN-CONTEXT REVIEWERS, ONE PER ROOT CLUSTER Round-1 verdict: REJECT on three cards, ACCEPT_WITH_BOUNDED_FIX on two, ACCEPT on two cheat sheets. BLOCKING FINDINGS, ALL VERIFIED BY THE PRODUCER AT SOURCE AND ALL APPLIED: BLOCKING QB2_A#q34: the card instructed candidates to deny that water mist lances and mobile water monitors are SOLAS requirements. VERIFIED TRUE against SOLAS II-2 reg. 10.7.3 read from the consolidated edition - 10.7.3.1 'Ships shall carry ... at least one water mist lance'. The card's own Trap Questions scripted the wrong answer. Fixed: the mandatory equipment is now stated with its regulation, the trap answers YES, and the draft/in-force boundary is drawn around the detection-and-control package only. | BLOCKING QB2_A#q34: the card denied mandatory hold drenchers and omitted reg. 19.3.1.3 entirely. VERIFIED TRUE - 19.3.1.3 requires cooling at at least 5 L/min per square metre by fixed spraying nozzles or flooding, drainage at 125% of spray pumps plus nozzles, bilge wells not more than 40 m apart. Added in full. | BLOCKING QB2_B#q15: the expansion carried through the very clause it was written to fix. VERIFIED TRUE against IMSBC 5.4.3, 5.4.4 and 5.4.5 read from MSC.268(85): cargoes ABOVE 35 degrees are trimmed too, and 35 degrees separates the 1.5 m and 2 m unevenness limits rather than separating trimmed from untrimmed. Replaced with the three-band structure. | BLOCKING QB7_D#q15: the card asserted there is no ISO standard for LNG and told candidates to answer 'none' when asked which ISO standard applies. VERIFIED FALSE - ISO 23306:2020 'Specification of liquefied natural gas as a fuel for marine applications' exists, and MIW's own QB1_A already cites ISO 23306. Corrected, and the correction STRENGTHENS the card's thesis: ISO 23306 also declines to set a methane number, leaving it to supplier and user by reference to the engine maker. | BLOCKING QB7_D#q14: the card reported MSC.551(108) as amending only 18.4.1.1.1. VERIFIED INCOMPLETE by reading all 26 amendment items - item 11 also replaced 8.4.1 and item 12 added 8.4.2 and 8.4.3, making an emergency release coupler / release system MANDATORY from the same 1 January 2026 date the card headlines, on a question whose second word is 'safeties'. Added to the currency bullet, to the safeties list and to the numbers. | BLOCKING both LNG cards: the source-confidence footers claimed closure over the IGF amendment set while MSC.475(102) and MSC.524(106) had never been looked for. VERIFIED - both retrieved from IMO's index and read; neither touches chapter 8, 18.4 or the BDN annex, so the conclusion survived, but the closure claim did not. Footers now name all five. | BLOCKING QB5_C_B#q9: 'it appears in the Quality Trilogy alongside Deming and Crosby'. VERIFIED FALSE against the corpus's own QB5_A#q7 - the Trilogy is Planning, Control, Improvement, and Deming and Crosby are separate theorists. Corrected. | BLOCKING QB1_FG_CheatSheet: after the 40-to-42 renumber the header still read 'Q1-Q40' and claimed to cover 'every question in the 2 Jul 2026 set'. VERIFIED and corrected - the same header-honesty defect the QB7_D cheat sheet fix had just addressed one file over. NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS APPLIED: QB2_A#q34: A-60 stated without its 3 m stowage exception; 19.3.2 paraphrase omitted 'or vehicle spaces' and the complete-isolation alternative; 'no DoC, no dangerous goods' overstated 19.4's carve-outs; IMDG currency stopped at 42-24 without naming Amendment 43-26 adopted at MSC 111. | QB7_D#q14: 'five things in writing' undercounted - the emergency actions are a separate written agreement under 18.4.1.1.2; and two statutory lists that the Code introduces with 'including, but not limited to' were presented as closed. | QB7_D#q15: the gloss asserting the BDN's storage-tank rows are the receiving side's condition was not supported by the annex and is now marked as a reading, not Code text. | QB1_F#q22: 60-second answer was over budget; torsional and shaft-power measurement was listed as common on almost any modern ship, which overstates it; and resolution MSC.428(98) - the instrument that actually makes cyber risk an SMS obligation - was unnamed on a card whose selling point is naming anchors. FINDINGS DELIBERATELY NOT APPLIED, WITH REASONS: QB5_C_B#q9 template deviation: the card uses ten headings where its eight siblings use a fixed eight-heading body, omitting 'Trap Warning' and 'Casualty Link'. Recorded as deliberate - Pareto has no casualty to link and inventing one would breach the no-fabrication rule - rather than forced into the template. | QB2_B#q15 pre-existing defects OUTSIDE this expansion's bound, registered not fixed: the reg-box cites 'SOLAS Ch VII / Regulation 7-1' as making the IMSBC Code mandatory, where the general hook is chapter VI and the DG-in-bulk provision reproduced in MSC.268(85) is VII/7-5; and the card's data-tags attribute carries authoring residue ('& 1: Dangerous Goods Section bulk **SECTION:** IMDG cargo') in a search-facing attribute. Neither was introduced here and neither is what this expansion was authorised to change. | QB1_F#q5 now contradicts the new q22 on digital twins and ML predictive maintenance - q5 presents them as standard fitment, q22 places them in the emerging bucket and names the opposite as a Common CE Failure. q22 is the correct one. Registered as a follow-up against q5 rather than resolved by weakening q22. | QB7_D_CheatSheet: the two new rows use plain Q-cell markup where the eleven originals bold the Q number. Cosmetic. PRODUCER VERIFICATION. Every BLOCKING finding was independently verified by the producer against the primary source before being applied - SOLAS II-2 10.7.3, 19.3.1.3 and 19.3.8 from the consolidated edition; IMSBC 5.4.3-5.4.5 from MSC.268(85); MSC.551(108) items 11, 12 and 26 from the resolution; MSC.475(102) and MSC.524(106) retrieved and read; the Juran attribution from QB5_A#q7; the cheat-sheet header by inspection. No finding was accepted on the reviewer's assertion alone, and none was rejected. Round-2 verdict: pending re-review.

cards.topic: LNG bunkering - the IGF Code chapter 18.4 procedure, the pre-transfer written agreement as amended by MSC.551(108), pre-bunkering verification, the standing conditions during transfer, the operational sequence, and the cryogenic, vapour, RPT and rollover hazards
cards.adjudication_note: Store classification confirmed on re-reading. QB7_D#q13 covers the leak and fire response and starts from an incident already in progress; QB7_D#q9 and QB7_E#q3 cover why the IGF Code exists; QB6#q10 is LPG. None teaches the bunkering procedure.

cards.topic: LNG fuel specification on ordering - the LNG Bunker Delivery Note in the annex to IGF part C-1 as the authoritative parameter set, the absence of any ISO 8217 equivalent, the single <5 ppm trace limit, and the methane number as an engine maker's contractual figure rather than a statutory one
cards.adjudication_note: QB3_F#q7 covers ordering fuel OIL for quantity and quality; QB7_I#q3 mentions a methane number of about 70 for Otto-cycle engines in a methane-slip comparison; QB8_H#q9 is LNG containment. No card covers what to specify when ordering LNG as fuel.

cards.topic: Preventing a container fire as Chief Engineer - declaration and segregation under IMDG, ignition-source control under SOLAS II-2 reg. 19.3.2 with the reefer electrical estate as the ship's own principal ignition source, and the reg. 19.3 readiness numbers; with an explicit statement of what is still draft
cards.adjudication_note: Resolves a contradiction in the store: AUG-0136 was GENUINE_NEW and AUG-0219 PARAPHRASE_EXISTING against QB2_A#q8 for the same ask. QB2_A#q8 read in full and is a response card - causes, EmS, firefighting - not a prevention card. Both occurrences recorded here; AUG-0219's IMDG limb is answered by the existing QB2_A#q9, which the new card cross-links.

cards.topic: Pareto analysis - the principle, 80/20 as a heuristic rather than a law, chart construction, the choice of measure, engine-room applications, and its limits against root cause analysis and risk assessment
cards.adjudication_note: The single corpus hit is QB5_A#q7 (TQM), where 'Pareto Principle (80/20) in quality' appears as one line in a table of Juran's contributions. That is a mention, not a treatment. The new card cross-links to it rather than duplicating TQM.

cards.topic: Digitalisation onboard, pros and cons - what is currently common separated from what is emerging, the advantages with their engineering reasons, the disadvantages including cyber risk and de-skilling, and the three regulatory anchors: IACS UR E26/E27, the approved electronic record book, and cyber risk inside the ISM SMS
cards.adjudication_note: Eight cards mention digitalisation. QB1_F#q5 is the closest and was read in full: it is a NEW TECHNOLOGY card - dual-fuel engines, shaft generators, OCCS, digital twins - and it advocates rather than weighs. QB1_C#q9 carries UR E26/E27 in a newbuilding-requirements context. QB6_F#q3 is blockchain. None answers a pros-and-cons ask, which is what the examiner set.

cards.topic: Angle of repose - definition, that it is a property of the individual cargo with no universal value, the 35-degree Code threshold correctly framed as a threshold, and the shift chain from low repose angle to permanent list
cards.adjudication_note: OVERTURNS the store's GENUINE_NEW_QUESTION. Seven pre-existing cards discuss the angle of repose and this one already owned the 35-degree marker; the adjudication's '0 hits over 738 cards, independently re-confirmed' is not reproducible and is contradicted here. The existing bullet was incomplete, not wrong, so this is an expansion in the batch family and NOT a correction - nothing false was published.
